title: Latency prober harness and flame collector scratchpad
content:
Purpose
---
Notes and a lightweight harness for reproducing short-lived latency spikes in the serving runtime, collecting minimal traces, perf flamegraphs, and a compact OpenTelemetry span export for offline analysis. This is not the canonical production collector but a small, fast-to-run harness intended for CI perf jobs and on-host developer triage.

Goals
- Provide a reproducible, small-footprint harness that exercises token generation hot paths (kv-cache hits/misses, attention matmul, kv-cache fill)
- Produce: perf flamegraph (both kernel+user), eBPF stack traces (user), and a small OTLP JSON export with sampled spans (100--1000 spans/test)
- Integrate into perf CI as a smoke/mini-regression job that runs in ~6m and emits artifacts to the perf-buckets/mini-harness/ folder

High-level harness architecture
- Driver: python harness that can run locally or in CI. Drives a pinned inference process via a simple HTTP/GRPC client with controlled prompt distributions and sequence lengths.
- Target binary: local debug build of runtime (instrumentation flags enabled) or docker image runtime:latest-debug
- Samplers: two fast collectors run in parallel
  - perf-based sampling: perf record -F 999 -g --call-graph dwarf -p <pid> -o /tmp/perf.data
  - eBPF stackcapture: small BPF program using bcc / libbpf to capture stacks on schedule and on syscalls that correlate with token emission (write/send)
- Tracing: lightweight OpenTelemetry SDK configured to batch and export to a file sink (OTLP -> file) for postmortem correlation with perf graphs

Quick start (local dev)
1) Build runtime with debug symbols and disable inlining (fast incremental build).
2) Start runtime with minimal config: RADIX=1, THREADS=4, KVCACHE=on, LOG_LEVEL=info
3) Run harness: python tools/latency_prober/run.py --mode=kv-miss-heavy --seq-len=512 --rps=10 --duration=120 --otlp-out=./out/spans.json &
4) Attach perf recorder to pid: perf record -F 999 -g --call-graph dwarf -p $PID -o out/perf.data &
5) Start eBPF capture (requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CI privileged container): sudo ./tools/ebpf/stackcap --pid $PID --interval-ms=30 --out out/ebpf.stacks &
6) Let test run, then stop and convert artifacts: 
   - perf script -i out/perf.data | ./tools/FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl > out/perf.folded
   - ./tools/FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl out/perf.folded > out/perf.svg
   - python tools/otlp_to_spansummary.py out/spans.json > out/spans.summary

Perf CI job sketch (circle/github actions snippet)
- Trigger: nightly perf-mini and on PRs labeled perf/mini
- Runner: dedicated perf-small runner with 4 GPUs disabled, 1 CPU group assigned for harness
- Steps: checkout, build runtime-debug (cache), start runtime, run harness (30s warmup + 90s sample), collect artifacts, upload to perf-bucket/mini-harness/$GIT_SHA/
- Expected runtime: ~6 minutes
- Failure criteria: any >3% regression in median p50 relative to baseline (baseline artifact lookup by GIT_SHA) or harness errors/exceptions

Heuristics for tokens/prompt distributions
- KV-miss-heavy: 30% short prompts (32 tokens), 70% long prompts (512 tokens) with random prompt prefixes to avoid cache hits bias
- KV-hit-heavy: repeat prompts with same prefix to encourage cache reuse; useful to validate cache lock contention
- Sampling for attention: sequences with long prefix + small new token generation (simulate chat turns)

Flamegraph tips and gotchas
- perf with dwarf call-graph is much better for inlined-heavy code; make sure -g and --call-graph dwarf are used.
- When using docker, run with --privileged or set CAP_SYS_ADMIN; otherwise perf loses stack traces.
- Kernel symbols: install debuginfo for libpthread and libc on CI image to get sane graphs (otherwise stacks end at syscall).
- Avoid combining very low frequency sampling (F < 400) with short runs — you'll miss hotspots. We use F=999 in most harness runs.

eBPF stack capture notes
- eBPF gives better visibility for user-space when perf is blocked by platform limits. We capture only user stacks on token emission syscalls to reduce noise.
- Keep buffer sizes small (4k samples per run) and write compressed output (.lz4) to avoid CI transfer spikes.
- Example flags: ./stackcap --pid $PID --event write --max-samples 4096 --interval-ms 25 --out out/ebpf.json.lz4

Trace correlation strategy
- Include a short random trace-id in harness requests and have runtime echo that id into a span attribute. This allows matching perf/eBPF stacks against the OTLP spans.summary by trace-id.
- Span structure: root span per request, child spans for kvcache.lookup, attention.compute, cross_attention.compute, kvcache.fill. Keep span durations coarse (ms buckets) to avoid trace explosion.

Artifact naming and retention
- perf-bucket/mini-harness/$GIT_SHA/run-$TS/{perf.svg,perf.folded,ebpf.json.lz4,spans.json,spans.summary,harness.log}
- Retain nightly builds for 90 days, PR runs for 7 days.

Common failure modes and troubleshooting
- Symptom: flat flamegraph (everything in runtime main) -> likely missing debug symbols or perf ran in kernel-only mode. Check perf record flags and container capabilities.
- Symptom: huge KV cache time spent but traces show no contention -> check instrumentation points: ensure kvcache counters increment and examine contention around locks (use perf lockstat).
- Symptom: eBPF crashes on CI -> lower sampling rate and increase stackcap buffer; ensure kernel bpf feature set matches local dev image.

Acceptance criteria for adding a new harness to perf-mini
- P95 latency measured by harness within historical baseline +/- 5% across 3 consecutive nightly runs.
- Artifacts present and viewable (perf.svg loads, spans.summary contains trace-ids).
- CI step completes within allocated runner time (< 10m).

To do (next steps)
- [ ] Add a small web UI for quick artifact browsing (perf.svg + spans.summary side-by-side) — Jonas
- [ ] Add a lightweight github action to kick off a diff against baseline and post a comment — Marina
- [ ] Harden docker build for perf with required debuginfo packages — Ethan
- [ ] Validate eBPF capture across ubuntu 20/22/24 kernels used in CI — Luis

Notes to self
- Keep harness scripts tiny; we want low-maintenance. Avoid full opentelemetry-collector deployment in CI unless we move to longer integration runs.
- Keep sample sizes consistent across runs; don't randomize seed unless explicitly running stochastic experiments.

See also
- tools/latency_prober/README.md (work in progress)
- tools/FlameGraph/ (upstream flamegraph scripts)
- internal doc: CONFLUENCE-RT-587: "Perf mini-harness design"

If you pick this up: start by reproducing locally with seq-len=128 and rps=5, iterate until perf.svg shows 2-3 distinct hotspots, then try kv-miss-heavy. Drop notes in #eng-runtime-profiling when you have an interesting flame.
